{{short description|Chinese physicist and science writer (born 1934)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Ni (surname)|Ni]]|lang=Chinese}}
{{Like resume|date=June 2022}}

'''Ni Guangjiong''' ({{zh|c=倪光炯}}; born December 29, 1934, in [[Ningbo]], [[Zhejiang]])<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://files.nyu.edu/jy272/public/ni.html |title=His profile on the New-York University website |access-date=2011-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120610023901/https://files.nyu.edu/jy272/public/ni.html |archive-date=2012-06-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref> is a Chinese [[physicist]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.tudou.com/programs/view/XoUarWJ4SaI/ | title=Recording of a participation in a television program }}</ref> He began studies in physics about 1950, and became a Doctor of Philosophy in 1955. He married Su Qing, a physics professor, in 1960. He published his first book in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.yurinsha.com/353/p6.htm|title=Guang-|website=Yurinsha |accessdate= }}</ref> He holds a Chair in Physics at [[Fudan University]], Shanghai.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rintonpress.com/books/gni.html|title=Presentation about the author at the Rinton Press WebSite|website=Rinton Press|accessdate= }}</ref> He is the director of Modern Physics Institute and the head of the Division for Theoretical Physics.

He is a specialist in quantum mechanics, field theory, and particle physics. His books include ''Modern Physics'' (1979), ''Methods of Mathematical Physics'' (1989), ''Levinson Theorem, Anomaly and Phase Transition of Vacuum'' (1995), ''Physics Changing the World'' (1998), and ''Advanced Quantum Mechanics'' (2000).

== Accelerating universe: the role of the antimatter ==
Ni is studied by several authors in astrophysics and for the theories of the antimatter,<ref>{{Cite journal  |url=http://www.infim.ro/rrp/2003_55_2/lazanMal.pdf |title=Matter-antimatter asymmetry of the early Universe and some elementary considerations about the space-time properties  |last1=Lazanu |first1=I. |last2=Malace |first2=S. |access-date=2011-11-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406035947/http://www.infim.ro/rrp/2003_55_2/lazanMal.pdf |archive-date=2012-04-06 |url-status=dead |journal=Romanian Reports in Physics |date=1 July 2003 |volume=55 |issn=1221-1451|osti=20386371 |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kmitl.ac.th/science/sci_journal/files/A_VECTOR.pdf|title=A vector model for gravitation field in curvature space-time |author1= Vo Van On|accessdate= }}{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> that he includes in the cosmological model that he proposes.

The theories of Ni about antimatter are also used for invariances of scale within the framework as Quantum tunnelling<ref>{{Cite journal |url=http://en.cnki.com.cn/Article_en/CJFDTOTAL-DXWL200602010.htm |trans-title= Some discussions on phase invariance |author1=JIANG Yong-jin|author2=ZHOU Xiao-yan|journal=大学物理 (College Physics)|accessdate=|title=相位不变性的若干讨论|volume=25 |issue=2 |issn=1000-0712|pages=30}}</ref> and it is within the framework of this cosmological model that Ni develops an important part of his study with regard to the neutrinos.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|title=Cosmic Ray Spectrum and Tachyonic Neutrino |first=Guang-Jiong|last=Ni |year=2004 |eprint= hep-ph/0404030v1 }}</ref>

==International works about a superluminal speed of the (muon) neutrino==
Ni claimed to prove that the muon neutrino exceeded the [[speed of light]] in vacuum. He spent most of his career studying this.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|title=Superluminal Paradox and Neutrino  |first=Guang-Jiong|last=Ni |year=2002 |eprint= hep-ph/0203060v1 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=A minimal three-flavor model for neutrino oscillation based on superluminal property |first=Guang-Jiong|last=Ni |journal=Rel.grav.cosmol. |year=2004|volume=1 |pages=137–148 |arxiv=hep-ph/0306028|bibcode=2004rgc..conf..137N }}</ref><ref>{{Cite arXiv|title=There might be superluminal particles in nature |first=Guang-Jiong|last=Ni |year=2002 |eprint=hep-th/0201077v1 }}</ref>
This work was cited on many occasions by international teams of scientists <ref>{{cite journal |year=1999 |title=Announcements |url=https://doi.org/10.1023%2FA%3A1018825405998 |journal=Foundations of Physics |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=139–141 |doi=10.1023/A:1018825405998 |bibcode=1999FoPh...29..139. |url-access=subscription |via=Springer}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nu.to.infn.it/Special_Relativity/ |title=Special Relativity |access-date=2011-10-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011144049/http://www.nu.to.infn.it/Special_Relativity/ |archive-date=2011-10-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in several anthologies.<ref>"Relativity, Gravitation, Cosmology, Contemporary Fundamental Physics" under the direction of Valeri Dvoeglazov, Chapter 12, page 149</ref>

== Distinctions ==
Ni received scientific awards recognized nationally in China, inter alia :
* Award of the worker models national (for his research) in 1979
* Progress Award in 1988 for state education delivered by the Commission of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Technology
* Progress Award delivered by the Ministry for the teaching of sciences and technology for a work on the theorem of Levinson left in 1995
* National outstanding commendation award of teaching in 2002 for a work entitled "world Change in physics"
* National award for the colleges of teaching and universities for a book about quantum Mechanical "advanced" in 2002.

Guang-Jiong Ni has also been quoted in the field of [[philosophy]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.god-does-not-play-dice.net/philosophy.html|title = The Doctrine of Trialism}}</ref> and by Siemens.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.siemens-cn.com/inductive-capacitive-coupling/ |title=Inductive capacitive coupling - Electrical information |access-date=2011-10-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425070114/http://www.siemens-cn.com/inductive-capacitive-coupling/ |archive-date=2012-04-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
